plain_english_policy: This bill authorizes Cherokee County to levy an additional one-cent sales tax starting when their current school-focused tax expires. The revenue is split: first funding School Resource Officers (SROs) in schools, then 60% of the remainder goes to the public school system, with the rest going to the county general fund. Crucially, this new tax requires voter approval via a referendum before it can take effect.
policy_direction_if_enacted: Enactment would create a permanent local sales tax increase specifically for Cherokee County, redirecting funds toward law enforcement presence in schools (SROs) and public education while providing general revenue to the county. The policy direction is increased funding for school safety personnel and education through a locally approved tax measure.
sponsorship_supports_position: Representative Lindsey (N & P) sponsored this bill affirmatively advancing the policy of increased local taxation for school safety and education purposes.
evidence_quotes: to authorize the county commission to levy an additional sales tax, exclusively for public school purposes

The proceeds from the additional tax shall first be used to fund school resource officers for Cherokee County schools, and 60 percent of the remaining proceeds shall be distributed to the Cherokee County school system, and the balance shall be distributed to the county general fund.
Sections 1 to 4, inclusive, of this act shall become operative only if approved by a majority of the qualified electors of Cherokee County
review_reason: The bill text clearly outlines the tax mechanism, revenue distribution, and referendum requirement without ambiguity.
